**1. TL;DR**

- Seven themes carry the tape.
- The market itself is not doing much: SPY +0.32%, QQQ +0.49%, S&P 500 futures +0.41%, and the median pre-market gap across 2,401 priced US stocks is **+0.14%**.

- **AI infrastructure is the lead theme, and it is a *re-rating* not a *reversal*.** Celestica (**CLS +10.87%**) blew out Q3 and guided 2027 revenue to $40bn;
- INNIO (**INIO +13.53%**) posted a record quarter with order backlog up **142%** to $8.0bn;

- The bid is for the demand narrative; the cash conversion is the part being discounted.

**2. Theme clusters**

**Cluster A — AI infrastructure: the financing-structure trade**

- **Leader: CLS (Celestica) +10.87%** — $273.47 pre-market vs $246.65 Monday close, 342.3k pre-market shares, $31.1bn cap. Q3 revenue **+83% to $5.83bn** (consensus $5.47–5.48bn);
- adjusted EPS **$3.30** (consensus $2.96–2.99), more than double $1.58 a year ago; Connectivity & Cloud Solutions revenue **+102% to $4.87bn**; record adjusted operating margin **8.5%**.
- Management guided **2027 revenue to $40bn** (vs $35.71bn consensus, +90% on the updated 2026 base) with adjusted EPS of $21.50 and a 9% margin, raised 2026 revenue to $21bn from $20.5bn and adjusted EPS to $11.55 from $11.30 —
- and **cut free-cash-flow guidance to $460m from $600m** on working capital, with 2027 capex of $1.5–2.0bn.
- CEO Rob Mionis: *"well-positioned to continue to support leading hyperscalers and frontier AI labs through the ongoing AI infrastructure supercycle."* An Investor & Analyst Day is held today.
- 23 of 24 analysts rate it Buy; Bernstein initiated Outperform with a $520 target. *Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/cls-stock-soars-premarket-blowout-081754257.html · https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9144188/celestica-cls-shares-surge-17-premarket-after-q3-earnings-beat-expectations*

- **Corroborator: INIO (INNIO) +13.53%** — $18.88 vs $16.63, 485.0k pre-market shares, $12.5bn cap.
- Record Q3: revenue **$1.2bn, +57%** (first $1bn+ quarter in company history), net income **$109.2m, +176%**, adjusted EBITDA **$245.4m, +70%** at a 21% margin.
- Equipment revenue **+86% to $777.6m** on large-scale data-centre deliveries; order intake $2.2bn; **order backlog a record $8.0bn, +142% year over year**.
- FY26 guidance raised to $3.9–4.0bn revenue and $780–800m adjusted EBITDA. Power delivered 1.2 GW. Call was 08:00 ET. *Source: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/27/3388791/0/en/innio-reports-record-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-with-revenue-up-57-net-income-up-176-and-adjusted-ebitda-up-70-raises-2026-full-year-guidance.html*

- **Corroborator: AVGO (Broadcom) +3.09%** — $339.33 vs $329.17, 653.2k pre-market shares, $1.57tn cap.
- After Monday's close, Bank of America, Blackstone, Citigroup and Morgan Stanley announced a **$63bn special-purpose-vehicle financing** to buy Broadcom XPU accelerators and networking gear and lease them to Anthropic, deliveries from 2027, with Broadcom providing residual-value support on the first-lien portion.
- Hock Tan is reported to have rescued the structure after lenders wavered. Anthropic's IPO filing disclosed **~$224.5bn of non-cancelable compute commitments** with Amazon and Alphabet.
- DA Davidson upgraded to Buy, $400. Counterweights: Alphabet diversifying TPU sourcing to MediaTek, and the stock still sits below its 50- and 200-day averages. *Source: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/10/62613053/why-is-broadcom-stock-gaining-tuesday-2 · https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/AVGO/news/*

- ORCL +1.50% · AMD +1.59% · NVDA +0.97% · AMZN +0.61% · TSM +0.50% · MSFT −0.63% · META −0.51% · AAPL −0.37% · PLTR −0.11%.

- **Interpretation and the caveat that matters.** The theme is coherent, well-sourced and broad — but it is a bounce inside a damaged month, not a new trend.
- CLS is −17% year to date and on its worst month in over six years; CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN were each down more than 35% in October before today.
- Two of the three cluster anchors are rising on *financing structures* (AVGO's SPV, INIO's backlog conversion) rather than realised cash.
- And CLS's own FCF guidance went down while its revenue guidance went up.
- The honest read is that the market is re-rating the probability of AI infrastructure demand, not the quality of the cash flows behind it —
- and the AVGO structure carries genuine circular-financing risk that several analysts have flagged explicitly.

**Cluster D — Private-credit M&A: MFIC +22.61%**

- **MidCap Financial Investment Corp (MFIC) $10.25 vs $8.36** Monday close, 663.9k pre-market shares, $688.6m cap.
- Ares Capital (ARCC) and MFIC announced a definitive merger agreement under which **ARCC acquires MFIC** in a stock-and-cash transaction for a **total enterprise value of ~$2.6bn**.
- Consideration is **$10.88 per fully diluted MFIC share**: ~$1.21 cash (from an Ares Management subsidiary) and ~$9.67 in ARCC stock —
- a **30.1% premium to MFIC's 26 October close** and a 25.8% premium to its 30-day VWAP. MFIC's preliminary 30 September NAV is **~$12.86/share**, so the headline consideration is *below* book.
- MFIC expects to declare and pay a **"meaningful" special dividend** of undistributed taxable income before closing, and the ARCC stock leg is reduced dollar-for-dollar by that dividend —
- so $10.88 is not the effective value per share. Apollo affiliates holding 5.2% signed voting and support agreements;
- closing is expected in **1H 2027**, subject to MFIC shareholder and regulatory approval; Wells Fargo agreed to provide $750m of additional secured financing;
- ARCC may issue up to ~41m shares (existing holders ~95% of the combined company). *Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ares-capital-corporation-agrees-acquire-100000340.html · https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/ares-capital-buy-apollos-midcap-financial-investment-26-billion-deal-2026-10-27/ · https://marketchameleon.com/articles/b/2026/10/27/mfic-arcc-acquisition-10-88-per-share-stock-and-cash*

- **Interpretation.** At $10.25 the stock trades ~6% below the headline $10.88, and that gap is *not* obviously an arbitrage:
- the special dividend reduces the stock leg, so the deal's true value depends on a dividend that has not been sized.
- The stock is also below its own $12.86 NAV, which is a normal consequence of a below-book acquisition and a warning against reading $10.88 as a floor.
- ARCC itself is **−0.75%** pre-market —
- the acquirer is not being paid for the accretion, consistent with the release's own "accretive to core earnings" framing being a guidance claim rather than a market verdict.
- Watch the Q3/NAV release on **5 November**.

- That is the single most important context for reading today's 46% and 19% prints:
- these are the tails of a momentum unwind, and they will gap hard in both directions again.

**Cluster F — Ferrovial: a concession-financing clarification (+9.79%)**

- **FER $55.28 vs $50.35**, 116.8k pre-market shares (thin — a Madrid-listed ADR; the Madrid line was up ~8%).
- Management clarified the financing and payment structure of its **I-24 Tennessee managed-lanes concession**:
- headline concession value of $24.8bn equates to roughly **$21bn in present-value terms**, with **$7.7bn of construction-period payments in 2027–2033** and a maximum **75/25 debt-to-equity** under TIFIA.
- That eased the capital-structure anxiety that had held the stock near its 52-week low (€42.77) and triggered a move in Madrid before the ADR opened. Context:
- an $8.9bn I-285 East Express Lanes win in Atlanta, a £1.5bn Anglian Water framework, TCI lifting its stake to ~13%, an €800m buyback extended to March 2027 (41% used), and rival legal challenges from ACS and Acciona.
- **Nine-month results are due after the US close today** with the call on 28 October; consensus is ~$0.32–0.33 EPS on ~$2.95bn revenue.
- Bank of America kept Buy with a €60 target (cut from €67); Deutsche Bank cut to Hold; JPMorgan downgraded earlier in October.
- The ADR is **not on Nasdaq's earnings calendar** — a genuine coverage gap for foreign issuers, and the reason FER's move has no calendar confirmation. *Source: https://www.perplexity.ai/finance/FER?comparing=FER,EN.PA,ACS.MC,028260.KS,000725.KS,EME · https://www.elespanol.com/invertia/mercados/20261027/ferrovial-abre-importante-hueco-alcista-pone-prueba-resistencia-euros/1003744435963_0.html*

**Deviations from the skill's procedure, stated in the body rather than buried:**

- **MCP layer absent.** The skill is written against `mcp__yahoo_finance__*` and `mcp__tradingview*`.
- Neither is registered in this runtime, so the cron prompt's public-HTTP replacements were used throughout: TradingView's public screener, the CNBC quote API, the Nasdaq calendar API, Yahoo, Coinbase/Kraken/CoinGecko and StockTwits.
- **No data was smuggled in from a prior session and no search result is presented as a live quote.**
- **The gap column.** The skill's Step 2 filters on `change`;
- in a pre-open pull that field is the prior regular session's move, so the gap tables use the pre-market column and Monday's session change is carried in its own column.
- Sorting is by the gap, matching the skill's intent.
- **Watchlist absent** — `research/watchlist.yaml` does not exist locally and 404s upstream. No default created. Section 6 states this.
- **Volume applied as a soft filter.** The discovery filter was price ≥ $10 and market cap ≥ $300m, with a separately labelled sub-cap section so that real movers are not silently dropped —
- a hard volume floor would have excluded legitimate names (MELI and AFYA were lost to one in a prior run).
- **Stale prints are published and flagged, not hidden.** Prints older than 45 minutes carry (warning) and their age in minutes.
- A stale print (GOOGN, 103 shares at 7:52 AM) was excluded outright because a live cross-check contradicted it.
- **Pre-open print volatility was measured, not assumed.** A second full read ~11 minutes after the first moved the median name by **0.00pp** (mean 0.13pp, max **2.26pp on DOCS**,
- which was −1.00% at 08:24 and −3.26% at 08:35). Single pre-open prints are not stable numbers; the spread is disclosed.
- **Crypto pricing was not taken from a single feed** after the CNBC index defect surfaced. Four venues were pulled and cross-checked.
- **No audit log was written** (Cloud cron instruction; audit is not required here).

- **Not verifiable at this snapshot:** the 08:30 ET durable-goods actual (Census 403; aggregators conflict), and any post-08:39 ET price.
- Several web results (Yahoo's, Robinhood's, Perplexity's finance pages) showed quotes stamped *after* this run's snapshot — those were discarded rather than published, since they are later-session values.
